title: Home recordings made in the twenties
summary: Blank-disc recordings at home of Mahogany Hall Stomp and Louis Armstrong numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you make any records in the twenties that weren't put out or anything?

Well we did. I mean when I was at Sam Colombo, they had a fellow who had a machine, a tape machine, I think it was, and we just got together, he'd come by your house or sofa like that, and we made records. But I don't know what I much did with it. Probably just for ourselves, you know what I mean?
This one must have been later though if it was a tape machine.
Well I had some kind of a box that we could go someplace and buy the record, the blank, you know, and we'd record what I did away with, you know, when I raised it here.
I'm telling you, it was real good.
What did you record? What tunes? Do you remember?

Well, Mahogany Hall Stump, and I know for sure that Mahogany Hall Stump in China Time, all that kind of numbers. I was pretty much playing all of Louis's numbers, he put it out, when you're smiling and so
